reference.method: mpmath at 60 significant digits, stored with 34

scenarios.name: Standard Normal
scenarios.title: Standard Normal upper tail, z = 1 to 40
scenarios.parameters: Mean 0, standard deviation 1; z in standard deviations.
scenarios.contract: 1E-13 in the tested region (standardized values up to 6).

scenarios.name: Exponential
scenarios.title: Exponential upper tail, x = 1 to 800
scenarios.parameters: Rate 1 (mean 1); x in units of the mean.

scenarios.name: Weibull
scenarios.title: Weibull upper tail, x = 1 to 28
scenarios.parameters: Shape 2, scale 1; x in units of the scale.

scenarios.name: Gamma
scenarios.title: Gamma upper tail, x = 5 to 800
scenarios.parameters: Shape 5, scale 1; x in units of the scale.
scenarios.method: regularized upper incomplete gamma Q(5, x)

scenarios.name: Chi-square
scenarios.title: Chi-square upper tail, 3 degrees of freedom, x = 1 to 1700
scenarios.method: regularized upper incomplete gamma Q(3/2, x/2)
scenarios.contract: 2.6E-10 in the tested region (cumulative and survival).

scenarios.name: Student t
scenarios.title: Student t upper tail, 5 degrees of freedom, t = 1 to 1E70
scenarios.parameters: 5 degrees of freedom; t in standard-error units.

scenarios.name: Poisson
scenarios.title: Poisson upper tail P(X > k), mean 10, k = 10 to 310

scenarios.name: Binomial
scenarios.title: Binomial upper tail P(X > k), 2000 trials, p = 0.5, k = 1000 to 1999
scenarios.parameters: 2000 trials, success probability 0.5; k a count.
scenarios.method: regularized incomplete beta I(0.5; k + 1, 2000 - k)
scenarios.contract: 5E-8 in the tested region (the loosest survival contract).

scenarios.name: Binomial LogPMF
scenarios.title: Binomial ln P(X = k), 2000 trials, p = 0.5, k = 1000 to 2000
scenarios.parameters: 2000 trials, success probability 0.5; k a count.

scenarios.name: Poisson LogPMF
scenarios.title: Poisson ln P(X = k), mean 10, k = 10 to 800

scenarios.name: Geometric LogPMF
scenarios.title: Geometric ln P(X = k), p = 0.5, k = 1 to 1500
scenarios.parameters: Success probability 0.5; k the number of failures before the first success.

scenarios.name: Negative Binomial LogPMF
scenarios.title: Negative binomial ln P(X = f), 5 successes, p = 0.5, f = 10 to 1500
scenarios.parameters: 5 successes, success probability 0.5; f the number of failures.
scenarios.method: ln C(f + 4, f) + 5 ln p + f ln(1 - p)

scenarios.name: Hypergeometric LogPMF
scenarios.title: Hypergeometric ln P(X = k), 2000 drawn, 5000 successes of 10000, k = 1000 to 2000
scenarios.parameters: Sample of 2000 from a population of 10000 holding 5000 successes; k the successes in the sample.
